newsitem.title: FRANCE: French growers see EU grain exports up to 30 mln T.
newsitem.headline: French growers see EU grain exports up to 30 mln T.

text.p: France's AGPB wheat producer association has raised the prospect that the European Union will export as much as 30 million tonnes of grain and products in the 1996/1997 (July/June) season instead of the 25 to 26 million generally forecast.
The EU has already granted licences to export roughly 23 million tonnes of grain on to the world market.

"Right now we are certain to make 25 to 26 million tonnes of exports on the basis of commitments. It is not out of the question to think, given worldwide demand and the logistical difficulties in Canada, that the final figure could be closer to 30 million tonnes," an AGPB spokesman said on Friday.
"That's what they think at the Commission," the spokesman said, adding the EU had exported a little less than 20 million tonnes last season.
The figures were not confirmed by the European Commission, which has refused since the start of the season to publish its grain balance.

The AGPB spokesman said the carryover of grains could reach 30 million tonnes at the end of this season on the basis of exports of nearly the same figure. After the 1995/1996 season, the carryover was 24 million tonnes.

"We will be at the low end of grain stocks needed in the EU," the spokesman said, estimating that need at between 30 and 35 million tonnes. "It's a level which would allow us to escape problems in case of a mediocre harvest."
The 1996 grain harvest is seen at between 202 million and 204 million tonnes.
Grain imports should drop to 4.5 million tonnes this season, which brings available stocks in the EU to between 231 and 232 million tonnes for the 1996/1997, the spokesman said.
He said the Commission was predicting animal consumption of grain in the EU of 104 million tonnes in 1996/1997, up from a previous estimate of 102.5 million tonnes.

Trade group Coceral expects animal consumption of 107 million tonnes. Last season animal consumption was 100 million tonnes. Non-animal consumption was estimated at 65 million tonnes, the spokesman said.
